children: BTCUSD slipped to $77,600 intraday, rebounded to $78,400 and hovered near support at $78,300; traders watch a weekly close below support and any bearish retest for downside risk.
Hyperliquid bought 500 BTC via ten 50-BTC buys in ~4 minutes (~$39.36M). Avg entry ~$78,639; unrealized gain ~49,300; 20x isolated leverage; liq price ~55,570 for BTCUSD spot CFD.
BTCUSD: ETF holdings and large‑holder accumulation rose. Buy wall at current prices. Binance reserves ~685–687k BTC. 7‑day net exchange inflows ~593 BTC. Stablecoin inflows to exchanges increased.
Year-end FX options show yen puts near 142.86. Rising yen funding costs and potential unwind of yen-funded carry trades may affect BTCUSD demand and liquidity as risk appetite shifts.
ARK Invest’s David Puell said BTCUSD’s on-chain SOPR rose above 1 but downside risk remains; he needs sustained SOPR >1 plus higher highs and higher lows in price to turn more bullish.
BTCUSD spot CFD: supply-in-profit at ~68%, above the long-term transition level (~64%) that historically preceded durable recoveries since 2012. Key metric for position sizing and risk.
Iran allows exporters to use crypto exchanges and pay for imports with Bitcoin and USD-pegged stablecoins, likely boosting on-chain flows and exchange activity affecting BTCUSD spot CFD.
Bitcoin Japan raised ¥9.7B in July 2026 and earmarked part for a Bitcoin treasury. BTCUSD spot CFD remains in strategy; custody, multisig, J-SOX controls and legal/accounting checks are in place.
Analyst on What Bitcoin Did linked U.S. long‑term insolvency and currency debasement to increased demand for Bitcoin vs US Dollar (Spot CFD BTCUSD) from investors hedging sovereign risk.
